prompt:
Platform engineering request for VCF 9.1. Build a PowerShell module named VksSupervisorAuth (VksSupervisorAuth.psd1 and VksSupervisorAuth.psm1) for the vCenter side of our VKS platform automation. It must enumerate vSphere Supervisor namespaces and manage the Supervisor workload Kubernetes API server settings, while allowing the vCenter credential/session to rotate without invalidating work that was already in flight on the old session.

Research before changing code. Inspect the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository for the VCF 9.1 vCenter automation contract. Confirm the exact operationIds, methods, paths, security schemes, response statuses, and optional UpdateSpec fields used here, and cite the specification URLs consulted in your final answer.

The environment provides VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager as a prerequisite. Declare it in the module manifest and use its real initializer cmdlets to export `New-VksVcfCredentialUpdateSpec -ResourceName -ResourceId -Username -NewPassword`, returning the SDK's CredentialsUpdateSpec for an UPDATE of one VCENTER API service credential. Do not vendor, shadow, stub, or redefine VMware.Sdk.Vcf or any of its cmdlets.

Export these additional functions:

- `Connect-VksSupervisor -BaseUrl -Credential`: create a vCenter API session with the documented Cis.Session operation and return an opaque client. BaseUrl is the scheme/authority (the module adds `/api`). Do not keep the PSCredential or plaintext password on the returned client.
- `Update-VksSupervisorCredential -Client -Credential`: create a replacement session using the new credential, then atomically publish it for future requests. Every request must acquire a session lease before sending. A request that already acquired the old session must finish with that same session; only after the last such request finishes may the module delete the retired old session. Never retry an old request with a new session, and never delete the old session merely because the new login succeeded.
- `Disconnect-VksSupervisor -Client`: stop new work, then delete the current session once it has no in-flight leases.
- `Get-VksSupervisorNamespaces -Client`: the Supervisor-based v2 namespace list operation. Preserve the returned array and identifiers.
- `Get-VksKubeApiServerSettings -Client -Supervisor`: retrieve the VCF 9.1 Kubernetes API server settings for that Supervisor.
- `Set-VksKubeApiServerSettings -Client -Supervisor [-CertificateDnsNamesToAdd <string[]>] [-CertificateDnsNamesToRemove <string[]>] [-NamespaceApiFairnessEnabled <bool>]`: send the documented PATCH UpdateSpec. At least one update must be supplied. Include a property only when its parameter was explicitly bound: unset fields are omitted, not serialized as null or empty arrays. Preserve caller array order and send snake_case field names exactly as the specification defines them.

Use `vmware-api-session-id` exactly where the specification requires it; session creation uses Basic authentication and has no request body. Every selected operation must send `Accept: application/json`; requests without bodies must not send `Content-Type`, and all JSON writes must send `Content-Type: application/json`. Treat identifiers as opaque path segments. Non-success errors must include the HTTP status but never credentials or session tokens.

Acceptance is `pwsh -NoProfile -File verify.ps1`. Do not modify `verify.ps1`.

research.language_rationale: VCF administrators commonly automate credential workflows with PowerCLI. The VMware.Sdk.Vcf module supplies the generated VCF credential models while a focused PowerShell REST client can enforce the vSphere Automation wire contract and concurrency-safe API-session handoff.
